description: A woman waits by the door with the patience of someone used to waiting out weather. Her clothes are road-worn but clean, and the gold hoops at her ears are the only things on her that have not faded. She came north with the salt caravans and stayed when they turned back, and she has the stillness of someone who has already decided what terms she will accept.
dialogue:
"I'm [event_worker]. I came up with the salt caravans and I'm not going back down with them."

"I've served road-houses from the coast to the passes. I can keep a full room fed and a difficult table calm, and I've done both on worse nights than you're likely to have here."

"I don't need the work sweetened. I need it steady. Tell me what you pay and I'll tell you if it's enough."

choices.option: Offer them a position for [COST] per day. (Potential: Reputation)
choices.message: You name [COST] per day. [event_worker] takes a moment, as though checking the figure against a road she has already walked, then puts out her hand. 'Steady,' she says. 'That'll do.' She is working the floor within the hour, and by closing she knows which tables tip and which ones only talk. Word gets around that you hired the southern woman who does not need telling twice (+5 Reputation).

She does not thank you twice, but she remembers it, and so does everyone who hears about it (+8 Reputation, +12 Relationship).
